values: Materials and setup｜All are editorially designed fictional data

You are doing a preliminary arithmetic comparison of photovoltaic options for a fictional rooftop project. P1–P4 are not measurements, quotes, meteorological data or a constructible solution; the formulas apply only within this exercise setting and are not a PVWatts simulation.

P1｜Both options use single 500W modules. Option A has 20 and option B has 24. The exercise equivalent hours are set at 1,200h per year with a uniform correction factor of 0.80, and annual energy is estimated only as capacity in kW×1,200h×factor. The preliminary target is no less than 10,000kWh per year.

P2｜The preliminary site limit is 24 modules, with costs of 60,000 yuan for A and 70,000 yuan for B and a budget cap of 72,000 yuan. Only one initial cost comparison is made here; with no electricity price, lifetime, operation and maintenance or financing given, benefits and payback cannot be calculated.

P3｜New shading information changes the uniform correction factor from 0.80 to 0.70, with all other settings unchanged. Recalculate both options and explain why the original recommendation changes; the P2 limit cannot be bypassed by adding quantity without authorization.

P4｜The design input V1 must be updated to V2, and the shading measurement, structural load-bearing, electrical protection, module layout and formal model validation all await verification; construction permits, inspection and grid connection approval have not been obtained. You can only submit the comparison and the pending verification list, the project lead decides, and professional design and review are the responsibility of the corresponding authorized personnel.
Tasks and outputs
Check capacity, annual energy, budget headroom and target per P1/P2; use P3 for the same-condition change comparison. For each result, write the unit, formula and material number.

List per P4 the input changes, the items pending verification, the corresponding responsibilities and the conditional recommendations; make clear that satisfying the target arithmetically does not equal engineering safety or permission to operate. Seal the first draft first, then look at the answer.
Reference answer (complete it independently first, then look)

Capacity for A is 20×500÷1000=10 kW, for B 24×500÷1000=12 kW. P1 annual energy for A is 10×1200×0.80=9600 kWh/year, for B 12×1200×0.80=11520 kWh/year; A is 400 below the 10000 target, B is 1520 above. P2 budget headroom is 12000 yuan for A and 2000 yuan for B, both within budget; initially only B satisfies the arithmetic target, the quantity and the budget at the same time.

P3 annual energy is 8400 for A and 10080 kWh/year for B, 1600 below and 80 above the target respectively; B is still within the arithmetic range but the headroom is markedly smaller, so condition sensitivity should be reported and shading verified, and achievement may not be claimed as guaranteed. Relative to P1, both decrease by 12.5%, not by 10%; the coefficient difference of 0.10 is 10 percentage points.

Paper calculations and version handover only; no climbing, wiring, contact with energized equipment, reporting of real returns or submission of construction drawings. subject.summary: Analyze sites, energy demand and solar system options, carry out photovoltaic or solar thermal design, performance assessment and technical review, and support installation and commissioning. The core output is an engineering solution with inputs, assumptions, calculations and version bases; design advice, construction implementation, professional signing and project approval each have their own responsibility boundaries.
